 The Other Sideline: Previewing the 100 Miles of Hate series in 2026
 Jeff Nations of Bowling Green Daily News sat down with Sidelines to give an insight into this year’s WKU squad. 
 Jacob Burgess , Co-sports editor 
 • 
 November 6, 2026 
 Ephraim Rodenbach WKU mascot Big Red dances during a timeout contest during a game against Middle Tennessee at Houchens-Smith Stadium on Nov. 15, 2025. 
 MTSU football is set to play the 76 th edition of the “100 Miles of Hate” series against Western Kentucky University and try to end its seven-game losing streak to the Hilltoppers.   
 Jeff Nations of Bowling Green Daily News sat down with Sidelines to give an insight into this year’s WKU squad.   
 “It seemed like they might have turned a corner earlier in the season,” Nations said. “Winning a couple conference games in a row but took a big step back against Delaware.”   
 MTSU quarterback Roman Gagliano faced the Hilltoppers in his first collegiate start last year.  Gagliano threw for nearly 400 yards with two touchdowns, but it wasn’t enough as the Blue Raiders fell, 42-26.   
 Rodney Tisdale Jr. led WKU to victory last year but has split time with Florida State University transfer Brock Glenn.   
 Glenn has been who the Hilltoppers have turned too since Oct. 8 against Missouri State University with a 2-1 record since then.   
 Head coach Tyson Helton   
 Helton was hired as head coach of WKU, three weeks after MTSU last won the matchup in 2018. Since taking over the program, the Hilltoppers have won by an average of 16 points per game over Middle Tennessee.   
 “The main thing is the points just aren’t there like they have been,” Nations said. “… Western is generally going to average the high 20s most year and they’re just not quite connecting as often as they would.”   
 Western Kentucky currently finds itself in the same situation as the majority of Conference USA, sitting at 2-2 in conference play.     
 Players to watch   
 Quarterback Brock Glenn   
 Glenn, a Covington, Tennessee native, is in his first season with the Hilltoppers after three seasons at Florida State. While with the Seminoles, Glenn played 16 games with seven starts.   
 The dual-threat quarterback has slowly taken control of the WKU offense, playing the majority of snaps over the past three weeks.   
 “He’s [Glenn] going to get the start, although Rodney Tisdale Jr., who was the opening day starter, is available at this point,” Nations said. “They’re just kind of riding the hot hand with Brock Glenn right now.”    
 Glenn is currently the team’s leading rushing with 451 yards on the season, which has been a struggle for the Blue Raiders to stop throughout the season.   
 Wide receiver Jonathan Stafford Jr.   
 Stafford Jr. is by far and away the best receiver for WKU, with 29 more receptions than Moussa Berry, who has 17 catches.   
 The true freshman has 433 yards on the year, averaging 9.4 yards per catch and 54.1 yards per game.   
 Stafford Jr. best game came against New Mexico State University, where he reached triple-digit reception yards on 10 catches.   
 Defensive back Jaylen Lewis   
 Lewis is the one player in the players to watch section who has been with the Hilltoppers for multiple seasons.   
 Another Tennessee native, Lewis leads the team with 64 tackles with 47 solo tackles. It carries over from last year where the redshirt senior finished second in tackles.   
 “Still a typical Western defense that gives up a lot of yards, limits the opponent’s points but not quiet as well this year,” Nations said. “… Jaylen Lewis has been kind of the guy that they’ve been leaning on as the anchor.”   
 Where to watch     
 The “100 Miles of Hate” will be aired on ESPN+ with a radio broadcast on WGNS Radio.
